title: INTRODUCTION TO COMPUTER SCIENCE 2
body:
The second half of first year, and the course where the training wheels come off. [[INTRODUCTION TO COMPUTER SCIENCE]] taught programming in Python; this one moves to C++, where types are declared, memory is yours to manage, and the program is compiled before it runs. Almost everything the rest of the degree assumes about how a machine actually works starts here: [[Pointer]]s, [[Stack and Heap|the stack and the heap]], [[Structure]]s, and the [[Class]].

The course runs on three tracks at once. One is the **language**: syntax, types, functions, control flow. One is **problem solving**: [[Algorithm]]s, [[Program design]], structure charts, testing, the discipline that stops you from typing before thinking. One is the **toolchain**: working over ssh in a Linux [[Shell]], editing in [[EMACS]], compiling with `g++`. The third one is invisible in the notes but it is half the work.

## Topics

### Coming from Python

```python
print("hello world")
```

```c++
#include <iostream>
using namespace std;
int main() {
	cout << "Hello World" << endl;
	return 0;
}
```

The differences that matter:

- Comments are `//` and `/* */`.
- [[main()]] is a value-returning function; it returns `0`.
- Indenting is no longer required (but still do it). Blocks are `{}`.
- A [[Header File]] `#include`s a [[Library]] instead of `import`.
- C++ is [[Compiling|compiled]], Python is [[Interpriting|interpreted]].
- Every [[Variable]] must be declared before use.
- Types are explicit, not inferred. See [[Atomic type]].
- A [[Function]] can return exactly one value.

### The toolchain

[[Workflow]] · [[Shell]] · [[EMACS]] · [[Directory]] · [[Bash file]] · [[File]]

Log in over ssh, navigate with the [[Shell]], edit with [[EMACS]], compile, submit. `g++ hello.cpp` produces `a.out`; `-o` names the output. Never name the output the same as the source, it overwrites your work.

[[Compiling]] · [[Interpriting]] · [[Machine Language]] · [[Hardware]] · [[Processor]]

Both compiling and interpreting are translation into [[Machine Language]], which is the only thing a [[Processor]] reads and is different for every processor. That claim is cashed out properly in [[COMPUTING MACHINERY]].

### Problem solving and design

[[Algorithm]] · [[Program design]] · [[Function design]] · [[Loop design]] · [[Structure chart]] · [[IPO Diagram]]

Polya's four steps (understand, plan, implement, evaluate) with the algorithm as the planning stage. An algorithm must be ordered, explicit, effective, complete, and finite. [[Structure chart]]s break the problem into tasks; the [[IPO Diagram]] pins down input, process, and output for each one. This is [[INTRODUCTION TO SOFTWARE ENGINEERING]] in miniature, four semesters early.

[[debugging]] · [[Driver]] · [[Errors]] · [[Compile Errors]] · [[Logic Errors]] · [[Runtime Errors]]

Top-down testing starts at [[main()]]; bottom-up testing starts at the leaf functions and needs a [[Driver]]. The three kinds of failure are the spine of the whole degree: the compiler rejects it, it crashes while running, or it runs fine and is wrong.

### Memory

[[Memory]] · [[Variable]] · [[Address]] · [[Byte]] · [[Pointer]]

A [[Variable]] is a name for a memory location. A [[Pointer]] is a variable whose value *is* a location, which is what makes indirection, dynamic allocation, and linked structures possible.

[[Static Allocation]] · [[Dynamic Allocation]] · [[Stack and Heap]] · [[new And delete]] · [[Dynamic Arrays]]

Static allocation is decided at compile time and lives on the stack; dynamic allocation happens at run time with `new` and lives on the heap. This is the entire reason `int numbers[x]` fails when `x` is read from input: the size had to be known before the program ran.

[[Variable Scope]] · [[Variable Lifetime]] · [[Storage Class]]

Scope is *where* a name is visible, lifetime is *when* the storage exists. They are different questions that beginners merge into one.

[[Call by value]] · [[Call by reference]]

Pass by value copies; the function cannot change the caller's variable. Pass by reference (`int&`) passes the location, so it can. The classic demonstration is `swap()`: it does nothing until the parameters become references.

### Data types

[[Data type]] · [[Atomic type]] · [[Primitive type]] · [[Compound type]] · [[Type casting]]

Atomic types hold one value; compound types ([[Array]], [[Structure]], [[C-String]]) hold many under one name. "Atomic", "primitive", "built-in", and "fundamental" are four names for the same thing; see [[Primitive type]] before a textbook switches on you.

[[Integer]] · [[Double]] · [[Float]] · [[Character]] · [[Boolean]] · [[String]] · [[Void]]

Integer arithmetic brings the [[Division Algorithm]] with it (`/` truncates, `%` gives the remainder), which in turn is what [[GCD and LCM]] and [[Prime Number]] tests are built out of. How these types are actually laid out in bits belongs to [[COMPUTING MACHINERY]]: see [[Data representation]], [[Integer Representation]], [[Boolean Representation]], and [[ASCII]].

### Functions

[[Function]] · [[main()]] · [[Header File]] · [[Library]]

Functions solve sub-problems, `main()` solves the main problem. You can use one without knowing how it works, which is *procedural abstraction* and the same instinct as an [[Abstract Data Type]] one level up. A function is **declared** (the prototype, in the [[Header File]]) before it is **defined**.

[[Parameter]] · [[Formal parameter]] · [[Actual parameter]] · [[Call by value]] · [[Call by reference]]

Formal parameters are the variables named in the prototype; actual parameters are what the caller actually hands over. Which one changes when the function assigns to it is entirely a question of value versus reference.

### Decisions

[[Descision]] · [[Conditional]] · [[Switch]] · [[Dangling else]]

`if` / `else if` / `else`, and `switch` when the conditional chain gets messy. `switch` falls through without `break`, which is a bug most of the time and deliberately useful the rest. Dropping the braces on a nested `if` gets you the [[Dangling else]].

### Repetition

[[Repetition]] · [[For loop]] · [[While loop]] · [[Do while loop]] · [[Nested loop]]

`for` and `while` are pre-test, `do while` is post-test and therefore always runs at least once.

[[Control variable]] · [[Sentinel]] · [[Counted loop]] · [[Finite loop]] · [[Infinite loop]] · [[Accumulator]] · [[Index]]

Every loop needs a control variable and something that changes it, or it never ends. A [[Counted loop]] knows how many iterations up front; a [[Sentinel]] loop runs until it sees a stop value, with `cin.eof()` as the file-reading case. [[Loop design]] is the checklist: what is the condition, how is it primed, how is it updated, when do you exit.

### Compound data

[[Array]] · [[Index]] · [[Parallel Array]] · [[Array Feild]] · [[C-String]]

Arrays are fixed size and known at compile time; declare a `const` for the size and use it everywhere. A [[C-String]] is a `char` array terminated by `'\0'`, so it always needs one more slot than it has characters. Parallel arrays are the bad version of what a [[Structure]] does properly.

[[Structure]]

A `struct` defines a new type by grouping fields. You can pass it, return it, and assign it, but you cannot compare two of them with `==`. It is the direct ancestor of the [[Class]], and the thing [[COMP 2ND YEAR/COMP 2655/C|C]] in second year re-explains from the machine's side.

### Classes and objects

[[Class]] · [[Classes]] · [[Object]] · [[Method]] · [[Class Relationships]]

[[Abstraction]] · [[Encapsulation]] · [[Abstract Data Type]]

An [[Abstract Data Type]] is a set of values plus the operations on them, specified independently of how it is built: you know how to use it, not how it works. A [[Class]] is how C++ writes one down. [[Encapsulation]] bundles the data with its operations, and `private` / `public` is the information hiding that makes the bundle worth having.

[[Interface]] · [[Implementation]] · [[Interface Module]] · [[Client Program]]

The interface is the promise, the implementation is how it is kept, and the client program only ever sees the first one. Change the implementation and nothing downstream breaks. That argument, generalised, is [[Coupling and Cohesion]] in [[INTRODUCTION TO SOFTWARE ENGINEERING]].

[[Overloading]] · [[Overriding]] · [[Copying]]

Overloading is same name, different parameters, resolved at compile time. Overriding is a subclass replacing an inherited method. Copying an object happens on assignment, on pass or return by value, and at construction from an existing object, which is exactly where shallow copies bite once pointers are involved.

[[Javascript Objects]] · [[Object Literal]]

A later addition from [[WEB DEVELOPMENT FOR CS]], kept here because it is the same idea without the type declarations.

### Dynamic data structures

[[Data Structure]] · [[Dynamic Data Structure]] · [[Node]] · [[Linked Structure]] · [[Linked List]] · [[Singleton List]] · [[List]]

A node is data plus a pointer to the next node, which is the trick that lets a structure grow at run time. A struct cannot contain itself, but it can contain a pointer to itself, and that one line is what makes linked lists possible.

[[Stack]] · [[Queue]] · [[Recursion]]

LIFO and FIFO, implemented here for the first time and analysed properly in [[INFORMATION STRUCTURES]]. Recursion is introduced at the end of the course; the reason it works is the call stack, which [[COMPUTING MACHINERY]] takes apart in [[Subroutines]].

### Input and output

[[Input]] · [[Output]] · [[Buffered Input]] · [[File]]

`cin` and `cout`, plus the buffer sitting behind `cin` that explains why input behaves oddly when you mix `>>` and `getline`.

## Core Facts to Know

- C++ is compiled; the whole program is translated once, before it runs.
- Python is interpreted; translation and execution happen together.
- Both compilers and interpreters translate to [[Machine Language]].
- Every [[Processor]] has its own machine language.
- `g++ file.cpp` produces an executable called `a.out`.
- `g++ file.cpp -o name` names the executable instead.
- Every C++ program has exactly one [[main()]], and it returns `int`.
- `return 0` from `main()` means success.
- Every [[Variable]] must be declared with a type before it is used.
- A [[Function]] returns at most one value.
- A function is *declared* (the prototype) before it is *defined*.
- Declarations go in the [[Header File]].
- Formal parameters are the variables in the prototype; actual parameters are what the caller passes.
- Pass by value copies the argument, so the function cannot change the caller's variable.
- Pass by reference (`int&`) passes the memory location, so it can.
- An argument passed by reference must be a variable, not an expression.
- An [[Array]] has a fixed size that must be known at compile time.
- `int a[n]` with `n` read from input is a compile error.
- Array indices start at 0 and run to size minus 1.
- C++ does not check array bounds.
- A [[C-String]] is a `char` array ending in `'\0'`.
- `char greeting[6] = "Hello"` needs 6 slots for 5 characters.
- The length of a C-string does not count the null terminator.
- A [[Structure]] groups fields of different types under one type name.
- A struct definition creates a type, not a variable.
- Structs can be assigned, passed, and returned, but not compared with `==`.
- Structs are passed by value by default.
- A [[Pointer]] holds a memory [[Address|address]].
- `&x` is the address of `x`; `*p` is the value at `p`.
- `char *p, q;` declares one pointer and one plain `char`.
- `new` allocates on the heap, `delete` frees it.
- Local variables live on the stack; `new` allocates on the heap.
- A struct cannot contain itself, but it can contain a pointer to itself.
- A [[Node]] is data plus a pointer to the next node.
- The last node's `next` pointer is `NULL`.
- A [[Stack]] is LIFO; the operations are push and pop, both at the top.
- A [[Queue]] is FIFO; enqueue at the back, dequeue at the front.
- Scope is where a name is visible; lifetime is how long its storage exists.
- `for` and `while` are pre-test loops; `do while` is post-test.
- A `do while` loop always executes at least once.
- A loop with no change to its control variable is an [[Infinite loop]].
- A [[Sentinel]] is a value of the same type as the data, used to mark the end.
- `cin.eof()` returns true when the input buffer reaches the end of the file.
- `switch` falls through to the next case unless you `break`.
- Cases in a `switch` do not need braces.
- An `else` binds to the nearest unmatched `if`, which is the [[Dangling else]] trap.
- A [[Compile Errors|compile error]] stops the build; a [[Runtime Errors|runtime error]] crashes the program; a [[Logic Errors|logic error]] runs fine and is wrong.
- An [[Abstract Data Type]] is a set of values plus the operations on them, specified independently of implementation.
- [[Encapsulation]] is bundling data with the operations on it.
- Information hiding is the `private` / `public` split.
- The [[Interface]] is what the client sees; the [[Implementation]] is how it works.
- [[Overloading]] is two functions with the same name and different parameters.
- [[Overriding]] is a subclass replacing an inherited method.
- An object is copied on assignment, on pass or return by value, and at construction from an existing object.
- An algorithm must be ordered, explicit, effective, complete, and finite.
- A [[Driver]] is a temporary `main()` written to test one function.
- Top-down testing starts at `main()`; bottom-up testing starts at the leaf functions.

## Related courses

- [[INTRODUCTION TO COMPUTER SCIENCE]], the Python course this one is the sequel to. Same concepts, no type declarations and no [[Memory]] management.
- [[INFORMATION STRUCTURES]], the direct continuation: [[Stack]], [[Queue]], [[Linked List]], [[Tree]], [[Graph]], [[Hashing]], and [[Time Complexity]] to say which one to reach for. Everything built by hand here gets analysed there.
- [[COMPUTING MACHINERY]], the same material from underneath: [[Data representation]], [[Integer Representation]], [[Byte]], [[COMP 2ND YEAR/COMP 2655/C|C]] as a translation table, [[Subroutines]] for how the call stack actually works, [[Assembly Errors]] for the same error taxonomy at the assembly level.
- [[COMPUTING MACHINERY 2]], where [[Pointer]]s and [[Memory]] become memory-mapped hardware.
- [[INTRODUCTION TO SOFTWARE ENGINEERING]], which takes [[Interface]] / [[Implementation]] and [[Encapsulation]] and turns them into [[Coupling and Cohesion]], and [[Driver]]-style testing into [[Unit testing]].
- [[OPERATING SYSTEMS]]: [[Stack and Heap]], [[Dynamic Allocation]], and [[File]] all reappear as things the kernel provides rather than things the language does.
- [[WEB DEVELOPMENT FOR CS]], where [[Javascript Objects]] and [[Node.js]] revisit objects and modules without the compiler.
- [[INTRODUCTION TO COMPUTABILITY]], which formalises what a [[Dangling else]] actually is: an ambiguous grammar.
- [[DISCRETE MATH]] for the number theory the [[Integer]] exercises lean on: [[Division Algorithm]], [[GCD and LCM]], [[Prime Number]], [[Sets]], [[Proof By Induction]].
